question: Recent journalistic investigations1 and academic studies2 have raised serious concerns by calling Meta’s impartiality in the 2022 and 2024 Italian elections into question.

They posit that, while the visibility of institutional messages on Meta was systematically penalised, that of right-wing and populist posts experienced an anomalous spike, resulting in the presence of Lega Nord content increasing by 140 % and that of pro-Donald Trump content surging by as much as 400 %.

In addition, the Italian Data Protection Authority3 has reported its suspicions that the ‘Election Day Information’ tool is being used for the purposes of mass profiling, a practice that could warp public debate and interfere with electoral processes.

Having regard for the DSA, which requires very large online platforms to mitigate systemic risks for democratic processes and uphold the transparency of algorithms: What dedicated audit measures is the Commission carrying out or planning to implement concerning the use of Meta’s election information tools to profile users?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.7.2026) Free and fair elections are at the core of democracy. The conduct and organisation of elections are the competence and responsibility of the Member States, in accordance with their constitutional and legislative rules, subject to EU law and their international obligations.
The integrity of elections and the civic discourse in the EU are a priority for the Commission, as set out in the Communication on the European Democracy Shield1.

The Commission has opened an investigation2 into the political content approach of the provider of Facebook and Instagram in April 2024, including into the suspicion that the provider may not have diligently identified, analysed and assessed the systemic risks to any actual or foreseeable negative effects for civic discourse and electoral processes stemming from the political content, as required by Article 34 (1) (c) of the Digital Services Act (DSA)3.

The Commission is determined to advance this investigation in full respect of due process. The Commission is monitoring the functioning of Meta’s services to ensure compliance with the DSA and has sent several requests for information, including on the topic of recommender systems.

To support the implementation of the DSA during electoral periods, the Commission issued guidelines4 to very large online platforms (VLOPs) and very large online search engines (VLOSEs) on managing risks related to electoral processes that focus, among others, on recommender systems.

Furthermore, providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs must also comply, where applicable, with the relevant obligations laid down in the Political Advertising Regulation5. Both legislations may apply in parallel to intermediary services which are involved in the dissemination of political advertising.
